ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended and in force; Executive Regulations of the AML Law issued by the Prime Ministerial Decree; Egyptian Central Bank instructions and Financial Regulatory Authority regulations as amended; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and its executive regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; and GAFI mandatory beneficial ownership register implementation rules requiring the filing of UBO data with the Commercial Registry system of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/National Identity Authority of the country of origin of the individual

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing / Incumbency for any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent governmental authority in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the corporate shareholder or its legal representative

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All shareholders / ultimate beneficial owners of the entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence screening against the Egyptian Central Bank sanctions list, Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority consolidated terrorist and terrorist-financing lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions, FATF public statements and enhanced due diligence lists, and to the extent applicable to international banking rails, EU and OFAC sanctions lists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require senior-management approval, enhanced ongoing monitoring, source-of-wealth verification, and documentation of the business rationale for the EOR staffing agency engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) online portal - Investor Services Gateway (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered company name must be in Arabic and comply with Arabic naming, grammar and commercial naming conventions. A Latin transliteration may be registered as a secondary/trademark-style name provided it corresponds phonetically and semantically to the Arabic primary name and does not change the legal identity of the entity. Names must not be misleading, immoral, inconsistent with Egyptian public order, identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, or imply governmental, military, religious or professional exclusivity unless lawfully authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection of a proposed company name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with GAFI's Name Clearance and Investor Support Committee at the GAFI Head Office in Cairo within five business days from the date of rejection or within the applicable notification period stated in the electronic rejection notice. The appeal letter or portal submission must restate the proposed name, attach the official name-reservation screening receipt, explain how the name is distinct and lawful, and include any trademark registrations, domain certificates or corporate authorization for sensitive words. GAFI must issue a new decision within ten business days of the appeal hearing. If GAFI rejects the appeal, the applicant may file a further administrative appeal before the competent Administrative Court (or the Economic Court for investment-related matters) within thirty days from the date of the GAFI decision, and may simultaneously reserve a replacement name in order to prevent delay of the incorporation process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible for an Egyptian LLC engaged in global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll services. The activity is a licensed manpower/staffing agency, and the Ministry of Manpower and GAFI require a physical, accessible registered office in Egypt, a professional letterhead, resident management, and local bookkeeping presence. A post-office-box-only address or a virtual office address without a locally hosted operational work station will not meet the statutory commercial substance test.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; approximately 70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first twelve months of operation, because licensed EOR/manpower activities, AML compliance registrations and payroll payment rails attract scheduled and spot-check reviews by the Ministry of Manpower, GAFI, tax collection authorities, and the Central Bank supervisory units through banks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Law No. 148 of 2019 (particularly Articles 1-10 and 39-46 on Limited Liability Company formation, capital, and incorporation contract); Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1981, as amended; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop (OSS) for company incorporation and commercial registration (gafi.gov.eg)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association (Memorandum of Association) filed electronically on GAFI Form 2, together with the Commercial Registration application and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Tax Card application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Law 159/1981 for LLCs; however, the entire issued capital must be fully subscribed and the nominal value of every share (hissa) fully paid in, in cash or in kind, at incorporation; cash subscriptions must be deposited into a temporary bank account opened in the company's name prior to incorporation (escrow-style deposit) and released upon issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the First Meeting of the Board of Managers, convened pursuant to Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended: FIRST, the initial allotment of the entire share capital is approved and the full paid-in capital deposited into the designated escrow bank account is confirmed. SECOND, the registered office at [address], Cairo, Egypt is formally adopted; all statutory books, corporate seals, and registers shall be kept there. THIRD, [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, and [Name] Financial Officer and Company Secretary, each with full operational authority and joint-signatory banking powers. FOURTH, the Managing Director is authorized to complete all license filings before GAFI, the Ministry of Manpower, and all competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Search Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation request selecting up to three candidate Arabic/Latin names, append 'Limited Liability Company' or its abbreviation, and pay the non-refundable search fee via the e-payment gateway; the system automatically screens identical and confusingly similar names against the Commercial Registry index; upon approval, GAFI issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI e-Form for name reservation
Copy of passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Proposed company name list (three alternatives in Arabic and English)
Board resolution or shareholder authority if incorporation is agent-assisted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Object in writing to GAFI's Name Committee within 15 days of rejection, submitting a new variation or a disclaimer letter from the conflicting company; alternatively, re-file with a revised distinct name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Notarization of the Incorporation Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE); Notary Public (Ma'mouria / Real Estate Registration Office) of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation account with a licensed bank and deposit the full subscribed capital; obtain a Capital Deposit Certificate stating account holder, amount, and purpose. Thereafter, present the incorporation contract and articles of association to a notary public for authentication: each founder or legal proxy must sign in person; the notary certifies signatures and annexes the capital deposit certificate and shareholder identification documents.
required_dossiers: Temporary bank account opening form and KYC package of all shareholders
Individual tax ID / VAT declaration of each founder
Capital Deposit Certificate evidencing full payment of the share capital
Draft Arabic text of the Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association (two originals)
Valid national ID or passport of each signatory
GAFI Name Reservation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries identity or attestation deficiencies, cure by executing a power of attorney before the same notary or by submitting translated and legalized corporate documents of foreign shareholders; minor defects are corrected without additional filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Application for Incorporation (Certificate of Incorporation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) — Investor Services Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit via the GAFI e-portal the electronic incorporation application with the notarized incorporation contract, the capital escrow certificate, name reservation certificate, and founder legal documents; the GAFI OSS validates compliance with Law 159/1981 and the Executive Regulations, settles the incorporation fee and stamp duties, and upon approval issues the Certificate of Incorporation and registers the entity with the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
Capital Deposit Certificate issued by the CBE-licensed bank
Name Reservation Certificate
Photocopies of national IDs / passports of managers and shareholders
GAFI application form signed by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: GAFI must state the legal basis for any query; the applicant has 30 days to supply missing documents and may challenge formal objections before the GAFI internal grievance committee, or re-submit after correcting minor statutory defects without duplicating paid fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) operated at the GAFI OSS; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Taxpayer Services Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the GAFI OSS completes the commercial registration and files the company with the ETA; the company receives the Commercial Registration Certificate and the electronic Tax Card with tax file number and VAT status; thereafter, the company must register as an employer with the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) for payroll-related withholding and social contributions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registry Form signed by owners
Tenancy contract of the registered office (lease authenticated with stamp tax)
Copy of ownership or usufruct title of the premises
Tax Card application and ETA registration form
No-objection letter from landlord and proof of property tax settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry or ETA issues a deficiency note relating to the registered office or tax classification, cure by producing an authenticated lease, paying outstanding stamp duties, or filing a written correction; an administrative appeal is available within 60 days of the adverse action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Contract in the Official Gazette and Trading Bulletin
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette (Al Jarida Al Rasmiya) — Ministry of Justice; Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and the Notarized Incorporation Contract at the Official Gazette office to publish a mandatory abstract of company particulars within 30 days of incorporation; pay the publication fee and obtain the stamped Gazette copy, which completes legal publicity and starts the limitation period for third-party objections.
required_dossiers: Certified extract of the Commercial Registration Certificate
Notarized Incorporation Contract (official copy)
Proof of payment of the publication fee
GAFI transmittal letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette queries the abstract, amend the text in coordination with GAFI and re-submit; failure to publish within 30 days is cured by written justification to GAFI and payment of late penalties, with re-publication within a further 30-day grace period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation, Company Seals, and Post-Incorporation Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of choice (CBE-licensed); GAFI One-Stop Shop for seal endorsement; NOSI for social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, Commercial Registration Certificate, Tax Card, and First Board Resolution to the bank to convert the temporary escrow account into the company's permanent operational account; order company seals; complete employer registration with NOSI within 15 days of the first payroll run; maintain statutory books (share register, minutes book, accounting records) at the registered office as required by commercial registration rules.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Certificate (originals)
Tax Card
First Board Resolution appointing officers and specimen signatures
Lease contract of the registered office
Bank signature cards and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Bank or NOSI queries on residency or signature authority are cured by ministerial attestation of the Board Resolution and apostilled/legalized identity documents of authorized signatories; renew any expiring certifications promptly to avoid operational deadlocks.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Manpower (MoM) — Manpower Mobility and Employment Services Department (Central Office for Private Employment Agencies)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License to Operate a Private Employment Agency (Permit for Employment Placement, Recruitment, and Temporary Staffing Services issued under Law No. 68 of 1988 concerning Private Employment Agencies and its Executive Regulations)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Low Impact / Registration only) — office-based administrative activity requires environmental risk screening and registration without a full EIA Report under Law No. 4 of 1994, Article 21, and its Executive Regulations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decree No. 92 of 2020 wastewater discharge limits for sanitary effluents to public sewers under Law No. 93 of 1962; no VOC or industrial air emissions permitted for non-manufacturing activity; periodic indoor air quality verification and municipal solid waste handling through licensed waste contractors

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate ('Ishhad al-Muqawama al-Madaniya') issued by the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) after on-site inspection; structural stability and building occupancy certificate from the local municipality; workplace safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, including office ergonomics, first-aid provisions, and work injury insurance registration with NOSI

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA | مصلحة الضرائب المصرية), a body of the Ministry of Finance; primary portal: www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipts gateway: invoicing.eta.gov.eg; governed by the Unified Tax Procedure Law No. 206/2020 and its Executive Regulations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Within 30 days of commercial registration at the GAFI One-Stop Shop, the LLC files Uniform Tax Registration Form No. 1 with the competent ETA office (online via ETA portal). Required bundle: legalized Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, Commercial Registry extract, statutory books, board resolution appointing a tax representative/statutory auditor, notarized power of attorney, and IDs of managers/shareholders. A non-resident owner must appoint an Egyptian fiscal representative. The ETA issues a single unified 14-digit TIN covering CIT, VAT, payroll tax and stamp tax. VAT registration is made on the same file within 30 days after the relevant VAT threshold is crossed; the taxpayer is then onboarded for e-invoice/e-receipt integration and obtains an electronic signature certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope / Tax_Exempt_Zone. The Egyptian LLC is a resident entity taxed at 22.5% CIT on worldwide income (Law 91/2005, art. 19 amended by Law 14/2020); non-resident and branch operations are taxed on Egyptian-source income only; no pass-through election. A company licensed in a Free Zone or the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) under Law 83/2002 may qualify as Tax_Exempt on export profits (0% effective CIT) where export conditions and customs supervision are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Egyptian law; entity classification follows the Civil Code and CIT Law. Available statutory choices: (1) Free Zone/SCZone licence election for 0% tax on export sales (Law 83/2002); (2) Investment Law No. 72/2017 incentive election (e.g., 30% deduction from investment costs for eligible sectors); (3) election to treat a foreign branch as a separate permanent establishment with transfer-pricing documentation; (4) VAT treatment election for reimbursable payroll advances to be excluded from taxable consideration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax (Law No. 67/2016 as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (Executive Regulation Decree No. 66/2017); voluntary registration: EGP 50,000; non-residents supplying taxable services to Egyptian consumers are registrable irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance of all B2B e-invoices and B2C e-receipts through the ETA interoperability gateway (REST APIs, XML/JSON payloads, HMAC signing, e-signature certificates). Invoices are submitted at issuance and must receive an ETA acceptance/cleared status before accounting effect; printed invoices carry a QR digital stamp. EOR platforms must integrate licensed payroll/ERP systems with the ETA API; non-accepted invoices result in disallowed input VAT, blocking of export refunds, and separate fines per invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (i) goods physically exported from Egypt; (ii) services rendered for non-residents and effectively consumed outside Egypt (Law 67/2016, art. 15). The EOR agency can zero-rate global contractor payroll, HR administration and compliance services where the client is a non-resident, the payroll execution and reporting occur from Egypt but the service is used and delivered to the client abroad, and the services are not attributable to a permanent establishment of the client in Egypt. Salary/social-insurance reimbursements are excluded from VAT when invoiced as recoverable advances with vouchers. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable in cash (Export Facilitation Program; refund timeline 30-90 days for certified exporters).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ACID/SAD) with customs release number (goods streams)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / courier consignment note evidencing physical departure (goods)
Commercial invoice + signed export contract naming the non-resident recipient
Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate (bank Swift/MT103/MT950) proving repatriation of export proceeds
ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoice with QR and acceptance code
Packing list, certificate of origin and insurance certificate (goods only)
For EOR services: service agreement, payroll computation and GL ledger, bank transfer confirmations (e.g., Wise/local direct debit), and offshore client records proving consumption of services abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may reassess and claw back zero-rated VAT within the general 5-year statute of limitation (Law 206/2020). Delayed tax carries 2% monthly surcharge; deliberate evasion triggers fines EGP 50,000 to EGP 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (VAT Law 67/2016, art. 72 as amended); forged or inflated export documentation attracts additional tax equal to 100% of the tax evaded, criminal referral, loss of export subsidy entitlements, and CBE penalties for non-repatriation of export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under the Central Banking and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, the official custodial authority for the Egyptian Pound, the sole licensing authority for authorized dealers, and the primary regulator of foreign exchange operations through the Foreign Exchange Trading System and the Banking Supervision Sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a fully liberalized, market-determined exchange rate regime for the Egyptian Pound as of March 2024 under the IMF Extended Fund Facility arrangement. Current account convertibility is broadly available across authorised dealers, including for service imports and remittance flows, subject to presentation of underlying invoices, tax compliance evidence, and standard bank documentation. Capital account transactions are convertible but subject to documentary verification, CBE administrative surveillance, and periodic liquidity conditions. Profit remittances from an Egyptian LLC require audited financial statements, a validated foreign exchange return form submitted through the dealer bank, dividend General Assembly resolutions, and an Egyptian Tax Authority no-objection/clearance certificate. Practical remittance hurdles include temporary interbank EGP liquidity tightness, hard-currency prioritization for essential imports, and heightened scrutiny of round-tripping where foreign shareholder loans are repaid within 30 days of inbound funding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As of March 2024, the CBE abolished all mandatory export proceeds surrender ratios and statutory conversion timelines. Under the pre-liberalization regime, 50-75% of export proceeds had to be surrendered within 90 days of collection; that regime no longer applies to invoiced EOR staffing service revenues. The Egyptian LLC is permitted to retain 100% of service export proceeds in a foreign-currency operating account with a licensed dealer bank or convert at prevailing onshore interbank rates. Nonetheless, the dealer bank must be in receipt of the underlying EOR service contract, delivered invoice, and a funds-received confirmation within 10 business days of settlement, and the company must maintain full CBE-form reporting to substantiate the source of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and Payroll Sweep Account
Operational Account and Cross-Border Denominated Settlement Account
Operational Account and Complementary USD/Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is LOW for an offshore EMI acting as the principal treasury bank. Egypt does not recognize foreign electronic money institution licenses, and the CBE requires all EGP-denominated treasury activity and related foreign exchange reporting to be transacted with a domestic CBE-licensed authorized dealer bank. Wise is usable as a purely supplemental belt for cross-border contractor payout corridors and for collecting small remittance balances from non-Egyptian clients, but it cannot hold the operational EGP corporate account, cannot perform CBE-mandated FX filings, and must be wired-through the licensed commercial bank account of the Egyptian LLC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence applies for all authorized signatories, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners. CBE AML regulations under Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended by Law No. 181 of 2022 require an in-branch biometric, passport, and specimen-signature interview for initial corporate onboarding. Remote onboarding or videoconference opening is not accepted for a newly incorporated, foreign-owned Egyptian LLC. Non-resident directors who cannot appear in person may be accommodated by granting a power of attorney to a resident Egyptian general manager or a licensed signatory; the power of attorney must be notarized, legalized by the Egyptian consulate in the relevant jurisdiction and officially translated, and the resident signatory still physically presents to the branch. The bank is expected to conduct a compliance site visit to the registered office address in Egypt during the onboarding process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material outbound payroll volume to Egyptian resident individuals without visible social insurance registration and with only generic payroll-aggregation records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: National Social Insurance Authority (NIO) registration certificate and month-by-month contribution schedules; personal identification copies of Egyptian contractors; written payroll mandate with specified beneficiaries, amounts, and disbursement cycles; employment and independent-contractor agreements with Arabic translations; corporate operational license and Egyptian Tax Authority registration; CBE-compliant payroll authorization signed by the local manager; bank reference from the payroll sponsor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border inbound wire inflows from multiple offshore client jurisdictions with mismatched purpose codes or without observable underlying trade invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed Global Employer of Record service agreements with overseas client entities; monthly commercial invoices with itemized per-employee fees and margins; client acceptance records and remittance reports; documentation of the ultimate beneficial ownership chain of the Egyptian LLC; three-month treasury flow projection that explains frequency and sizes of receivable entries; investor and client bank reference letters from an internationally recognized institution; CBE purpose-code declaration for each inbound stream.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rebate or fee pass-through loan repayment from a foreign parent shortly after capital injection, triggering suspicion of round-tripping or unregistered foreign borrowing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI foreign investment registration certificate issued under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; notarized and consular-attested Articles of Association and board capital injection resolution; source-of-wealth accounting of the parent company; original inward remittance certificate issued by the receiving dealer bank; shareholder loan agreement with interest calculation, repayment schedule and tax-registration filings; audited financial statements proving the repayment corresponds to distributable profits or board-approved intercompany settlement; repatriation form filed through the CBE dealer bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Organizational structure of foreign directors residing in low-tax jurisdictions with no local directorial substance, triggering sanction and fit-and-proper review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attested directors' passports and CVs; residence visas and certification of foreign identity documents; UAE/BVI/Singapore business-license extracts and tax-residence certificates for outside directors; Egyptian commercial register entry stating the LLC's legal manager; appointment of a local auditor and local compliance officer; notarized physical office lease and utility records proving substance; written undertaking to provide semi-annual substance declarations to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound foreign direct investment and intercompany working capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 through a CBE-licensed dealer bank to the LLC's capital or operational account. The instruction fields must reflect the appropriate Egyptian FX purpose code (foreign direct investment equity code for paid-in capital, intercompany loan or service-advance code for operational funding), together with the transferring entity's name, country of origin, and a narration referencing the investment registration number or underlying service agreement. The receiving bank will file the prescribed CBE form and generate an inward remittance certificate that must be kept for GAFI, CBE, and corporate tax records. The LLC must then register the inflow with GAFI under Investment Law 72 of 2017, and for any conversion into Egyptian Pounds it must deal with the onshore open market through the dealer bank. Rebate or excess payments from offshore clients must be classified with the correct service-trade purpose code and supported by the corresponding EOR invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local payroll and contractor disbursements in Egypt are executed via the CBE-operated Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system, the automated clearing house (ACH) rail, or Meeza card scheme where contracting parties hold Meeza prepaid/in-payment credentials; each disbursement requires a pre-uploaded payroll file and a valid direct debit mandate. Foreign-currency payments for subcontractors, healthcare admin, or regional vendor settlements follow SWIFT MT103 rules with full COR/COR beneficiary-account formatting, based on reimbursement or disbursal invoices, and with the supporting FX application (outward report) required by CBE circulars. For larger or extended payment terms to non-Egyptian suppliers, a Commercial Letter of Credit (CL/C) pursuant to UCP 600 or a Standby Letter of Credit may be issued by the Egyptian dealer bank as primary settlement rail. All foreign-currency payments require a present tax-status check against withholding obligations and the issuance of the appropriate CBE-required payment order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable fuel-hedge foreign exchange forwards with tenors up to 12 months, executed on a hedge-only basis with a CBE-licensed dealer bank and supported by a documented underlying payroll or trade exposure
FX swaps (spot-versus-forward double-leg transactions) contracted with an authorized dealer bank to manage temporary working capital currency mismatches
Plain-vanilla currency options, call or put, in USD/EGP or EUR/EGP, when offered and approved by the dealer bank and the CBE treasury desk for treasury hedging only

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP used exclusively to hedge exposures that cannot be covered in the onshore market, with settlement in USD/EUR through an internationally recognized counterparty bank and with the hedging rationale documented to the CBE on request
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated EGP-denominated financing liabilities, subject to prior CBE approval and full disclosure of underlying debt service obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement and cash flow)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; by 30 April for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly late-payment surcharge plus fixed administrative fine for late filing; forced tax assessment and bank-account attachment on sustained default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the company commercial registry record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry / GAFI One-Stop Shop, Ministry of Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within one month of the registration anniversary and no later than 30 June each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EGP 10,000 for each un-renewed registry year; prolonged non-renewal deletes the registry record and blocks banking, customs and payroll operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner (UBO) confirmation and UBO register update for the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Corporate Registration Sector (Companies Law 159/1981 as amended; AML Law 80/2002)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the preceding calendar year; within 30 days after any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000 under AML enforcement; registration freeze and director disqualification for concealment of share transfers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the manpower / employment-services licence required for ISIC 7810 EOR and staffing activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Manpower - Employment Services Licensing Directorate (Unified Labour Law 12/2003)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before licence expiry each year; renewal window opens 60 days prior to expiration with no automatic grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines, suspension or revocation of the licence; administrative closure of staffing operations and criminal liability of the manager for unlicensed labour supply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social-insurance wage/scale declaration with the monthly contribution settlement summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration by 31 January for the preceding year; monthly contributions due by the 15th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 8% per-annum late-payment surcharge; criminal fines for false declarations and personal liability of the LLC manager on default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for all companies irrespective of size: the LLC must appoint at least one statutory auditor (licensed Egyptian CPA) at the annual general meeting; audited financial statements must be attached to the corporate income tax return
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), an IFRS-converged national framework issued by the Ministry of Investment; consolidated groups apply the EAS on consolidation and supplementary FRA/CBE reporting rules where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the GAFI UBO regime, the LLC must identify all beneficial owners holding 25% or more directly or indirectly, maintain an updated UBO register at the registered office, confirm it during the annual statutory audit, and file any updated UBO schedule with GAFI within 30 days of a share transfer; the annual UBO confirmation is bundled with the commercial registry renewal cycle
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Managers of the LLC)
UBO Register (Beneficial Owner register required by GAFI / AML Law 80/2002)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt grants preferential CIT treatment under the Investment Law No. 72/2017, including: (i) a 30–50% reduction of taxable income for qualifying projects in underdeveloped governorates or establishing companies with capital intensity; (ii) Free Zone status on exported goods and services with full CIT exemption, replaced by an annual 1% fee on total export/import throughput; and (iii) additional investment allowances for Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) strategic projects.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return – Form No. 35 (as prescribed under Law No. 91/2005); filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (inaysah.ata.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within 4 months of the end of the fiscal year, irrespective of the year-end date chosen by the company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian Tax Card registration number issued to the Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) of the foreign legal entity; if no PE, do not file for Egyptian-source income via Form 35.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period, fiscal year-end date, and accounting standard used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the PE's accounting records; foreign-head-office accounting calendar must match the Egyptian PE's audited statements for consistency in treaty parameters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and sales from services (including global EOR activity, payroll pass-through amounts, and contractor remuneration).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egyptian-sourced gross revenue attributable to the PE must be declared; intercompany service fees to foreign head office may be deductible if arm's length and supported by TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of services rendered, including salaries, benefits, contractor payouts, and direct payroll costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible to the PE only if actually incurred in producing taxable income; reimbursed payroll expenses should be supported by payroll records and employment contracts under Egyptian labor law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, utilities, marketing, professional fees, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head office overhead allocations must conform to Article 41 of Law 91/2005 and Egypt's TP regulations; non-supported allocations are disallowed and attract 20% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on intercompany or external borrowings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest must satisfy thin capitalization rules under Egyptian TP guidelines; excessive interest deductions are reclassified and subjected to 20% WHT on remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalties, technical service fees, management fees, and payments to related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only arm's length, economically substantiated payments are deductible. Rendering foreign services into Egypt without a PE may create Egyptian-source income subject to 20% WHT/TP review.
Derived from the PE's standalone Egyptian statutory financial statements prepared in Egyptian pounds and closing at the Egyptian fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back schedule: disallowed expenses, non-deductible provisions, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document any TP adjustments made by the foreign head office; unilateral adjustments are not recognized absent an approved bilateral APAs with Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, capital allowances, and investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions in genuine PE-profit attribution only if the PE has economic substance; otherwise profits may be recharacterized as fully Egyptian-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT due at 22.5% on taxable income before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No transitional exemption for non-resident-owned EOR; minimum tax on taxable income may apply if statutory rate yields lower than 22.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: foreign tax credits, quarterly prepayments, and excess withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit is allowed for Egyptian WHT withheld on domestic-source income only; foreign tax credits are regulated by the DTA and require valid TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds to non-residents are processed after ETA audit; bank account in Egypt must be active, and a refund agent may be required for non-resident entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 35 triggers an additional monthly penalty of 1.0% of the tax due, capped at 50% (Article 38 of Law 91/2005, as amended by Law 173/2020); late payment incurs a 2% monthly delinquency penalty; e-filing non-compliance may lead to an administrative fixed fine between EGP 5,000 and EGP 50,000; failure to submit statutory financial statements with the return may result in a penalty equal to 5% of taxable income (minimum EGP 10,000).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Estimated Corporate Tax Payment – Form No. 22 (e-filing via ETA portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Interim payments are due on the last day of the fourth month following the start of each quarterly period (i.e., 30 April, 30 July, 31 October, 31 January depending on the fiscal year chosen), with final settlement in the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer account numbers and relevant fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE's Egyptian Tax Card number and ensure the foreign head office name does not appear unless separately registered for WHT obligations.
Base the estimate on the prior year's audited return and current-year cash basis projections for EOR fee income; conservative estimates avoid underpayment punitive interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed quarterly prepayment (22.5% of estimated taxable income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No favorable prepayment regime for non-residents; the PE must pay in Egyptian pounds and may net against WHT credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of quarterly prepayments by more than 20% triggers interest at the Egyptian treasury rate plus 2 percentage points; failure to submit Form 22 incurs a fixed penalty of EGP 5,000 plus a 1% monthly surcharge on underpaid amounts until filing date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced DTA withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must (i) certify beneficial ownership via a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty state; (ii) submit a Form 'DTA Application' to the Egyptian Tax Authority within 30 days before the dividend distribution date; (iii) obtain an advance clearance from ETA's Central Division of International Taxation; and (iv) attach the clearance and TRC to the annual payroll of withholding statements. Absent clearance, the paying company must withhold the statutory 10% and the excess is generally refundable only through treaty mutual agreement procedure (MAP).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT rates are 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-residents. Under Egypt's network of DTAs, royalties are typically reduced to 10–15% and interest to 10–15%, provided that (i) the recipient is a beneficial owner resident in the treaty state, (ii) TRC is current, and (iii) the payment is not attributable to a permanent establishment in Egypt. Technical service fees and management fees are treated separately and may carry 20% WHT where no DTA provision exists; a growing number of treaties apply a 12.5% or 10% cap on such fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File requirement arises when the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 10 million in a tax period; a Master File is required when the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 150 million or when the annual value of related-party transactions with Egyptian entities exceeds EGP 30 million. Simplified documentation (summary TP form) applies for transactions between EGP 5 million and EGP 10 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code similar to UAE/Bahrain, but the Egyptian Tax Authority applies the OECD BEPS substance-over-form principle, the anti-abuse clause in Article 56 of Law 91/2005, and GAAR measures to deny treaty benefits to shell or letter-box companies. A PE of a foreign EOR platform must demonstrate actual people, physical premises, payroll records, bank accounts, and decision-making capacity in Egypt; free-zone companies must meet minimum substance thresholds in the relevant investment zones under Investment Law 72/2017 and may be subject to annual 'economic presence' checks. Failure of substance tests leads to reclassification of profit as fully Egyptian-source and disqualification from DTA relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Egyptian-sourced EOR revenues, understating taxable profit, fabricating payroll invoices, or using offshore shell entities to conceal taxable service income attributable to the Egyptian PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines equal to 200% of the underpaid tax plus double the tax due; criminal imprisonment for up to 5 years under Article 391 of Law 91/2005 and the Criminal Code; the tax authority may issue an administrative seizure of bank accounts and assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Egyptian LLC are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid tax debts where the under-declaration was intentional or caused by gross negligence; courts may issue travel bans and asset freezes; personal imprisonment of officers (up to 3 years) is available if criminal intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance in the Egyptian PE
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Egyptian existence with no physical presence, no personnel except a registered manager, no local service assets, and routing all billing and payroll through a Mauritius or Dubai intermediate without substantive operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entire EOR fee as Egyptian-source profit subject to 22.5% CIT plus 10–20% WHT; additional 50% ex officio assessment under Article 49 of Law 91/2005; denial of treaty benefits and double exclusion or inclusion of profits with penal interest at 2% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the additional tax and penalties if they sign or cause to be signed declarations misrepresenting the PE's substance; administrative enforcement includes entry bans for pure-letter-box directors found to have exercised control from Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare Local File / Master File despite exceeding EGP 10 million thresholds, charging non-arm's length global EOR fees to the Egyptian PE, or financing the PE with excessive shareholder debt without adequate interest expense allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of excess interest and service fees; TP adjustment back-calculated using Egyptian comparables; penalty of 10–40% of the adjusted tax difference; exposure to APAs and mutual agreement relief is revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability for the resulting tax shortfall if they knowingly approved the transfer-pricing arrangements; repeated violations trigger disqualification from board positions in Egyptian companies and police travel bans during tax ex officio proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Suspicious Cross-Border Payments Evading Withholding Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Egyptian EOR payroll and contractor payments through personal bank accounts in foreign tax havens, splitting payments below WHT thresholds, or failing to register the foreign head office as a beneficiary of Egyptian-source interest, royalty, or fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian Central Bank AML rules and Criminal Procedure Code, financial transactions in excess of EGP 100,000 per movement are reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); deliberate evasion is punishable with imprisonment (3–7 years) and fines up to EGP 500,000; the underlying corporate transaction is nullified and the withheld tax becomes immediately due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are individually liable for failing to prevent money laundering; the Egyptian Central Bank may revoke the EOR entity's payment/remittance license, and directors face seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing and Non-Payment of Interim Corporate Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the statutory 4-month filing deadline or failing to pay quarterly prepayments on Form 22 with no agreed asset-freeze waiver or force-majeure relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monthly 1% penalty on tax due (capped at 50%) plus 2% monthly delinquency surcharge; interest accruing at the Central Bank discount rate + 2%; remedial seizure of accounts and property through ETA collection departments after 60 days of non-payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the company remains in default and the directors had personal knowledge of the accrued tax liability, they may become personally liable for the unpaid amount under the 'piercing the veil' doctrine in Article 25 of Law 91/2005, and the competent court may issue a travel suspension.
